title: Towards Efficient Load Balancing BFS on GPUs: One Code for AMD, Intel & Nvidia
problem: Breadth-first search (BFS) on GPUs suffers from poor load balancing and memory access patterns; writing efficient BFS for heterogeneous GPUs (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel) requires multiple codebases
motivation: Graph processing is critical for many applications; BFS is fundamental algorithm. Existing implementations suboptimal on specific GPU types; portability across GPU vendors requires significant effort due to language and API differences.
method: Three GPU-based load-balancing methods using Intel oneAPI/SYCL: (1) work-group localisation for efficient data access, (2) even workload distribution for higher GPU occupancy, (3) hybrid strided-access for heuristic balancing; unified codebase for AMD MI300X, Intel Max 1550, NVIDIA A100
key_novelty: First unified BFS implementation achieving high performance and portability across AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA GPUs using SYCL; novel load-balancing strategies enabling competitive performance
contributions: Work-group localisation strategy for spatial data locality
Unified SYCL codebase for three GPU vendors
Peak performance: 153.27 GTEPS on A100 (8 GPUs, RMAT25-64)
Scalability: Handles RMAT graphs up to scale 29

metrics.scalability: Handles RMAT graphs up to scale 29

limitations: Limited comparison across GPU types (mostly results on A100); specific performance on AMD and Intel GPUs not detailed in abstract; real-world dataset performance secondary to synthetic graphs
primary_theme: Portable GPU Programming for Graph Algorithms
